pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher's Welcome - Holy Family Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
We value working closely with parents, our parish and diocese, as we believe children develop into the best version possible of the person God intended them to be when everyone is working together. Our ambitious mission statement, 'Trying to Make the World a Better Place', reflects our determination to live out the Gospel values, in solidarity with those less fortunate than ourselves, and to strive for the Common Good.
At the heart of our education is a child-centred approach. We appreciate that every child is unique, and we endeavour to know them as individuals. We recognise and celebrate the dignity of everyone in our community to ensure our school is fully inclusive. By making the curriculum and learning experiences active, creative and diverse, we nurture a love of learning and a passion to continue education throughout their lives.
Well-respected by local authority officers and school inspectors, we are proud to have achieved: consistently high academic standards, outstanding inspection reports, a reputation for excellent pastoral support and close partnership with local schools.
On September 1st 2024, Holy Family Catholic School joined St Thomas Catholic Academies Trust. We enjoy forging strong relationships with colleagues and capitalising on new opportunities as they arise.
If you wish to know more, or see for yourself what a special school Holy Family is, please make an appointment to visit. Tours for prospective parents take place on the first Wednesday of every month and every Wednesday throughout November; please contact the school office to book a tour.
Mrs Sara Benn Headteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: SEND Information - Holy Family Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
SEND Information
Children are a gift from the Lord; they are a real blessing.
We believe our school should be a happy and caring place where children want to come and where they can feel secure. As teachers we aim to create an environment in which children can experience the joy of learning, are valued as important members of the school and belong to a community that celebrates their differences.
We recognise that each child is of equal value and that it is our privilege and responsibility to accept each child into our community. Beginning from their first day and throughout their stay with us, we should have high expectations of all children in order to encourage them to develop their potential to the full.
We believe that every individual in the school should be accorded the respect and dignity that is the right of every person. In all our relationships, we should be fair, consistent, encouraging, understanding and compassionate.
We believe that education is a shared responsibility of parents, teachers, the Church and community. Parents have a right to expect that what a child is taught is what a child needs to know and that education should develop a sense of self-respect and the capacity to live as independent, self-motivated people with the ability to function as contributing members of co-operative groups.
Our SENDCo can be reached at Louise.Clarke@HFCS.org.uk
Our SEND Policy and other relevant documents can be found below:

pageCache.pageTitle: Before & After School Care  - Holy Family Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Before & After School Care
Early Birds & Sunset Owls (School)
Rising Robins & Sleepy Sparrows (Nursery)
We are mindful of the pressures that many parents experience in attempts to manage both professional and family commitments and therefore we offer before and after school care, available from 7:45am until 5:45pm. Your child will be looked after by familiar adults in a safe and appropriate environment, and younger school children will be taken to and from their classrooms in time for registration in the morning and collected again at the end of the day. Nursery children will stay in their usual, familiar setting. Breakfast is provided in the morning session until 8:15am, and snacks are available for those attending after school. A range of activities are provided in both before and after school care, and children enjoy spending time with other children from across school from Reception to Year 6, and staying with their peer group if they attend our Nursery. If you choose to use this service, there is no need to commit to every day, or to both before and after school care. Simply indicate on the forms what your requirements are and we will do our best to accommodate your needs. In order to ensure the safety of all children at all times, we do operate a strict policy in regards to drop off and pick-up times; we are sure you understand the importance of maintaining this policy. Please download and complete the forms below:

pageCache.pageTitle: Safeguarding Information For Parents - Holy Family Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Safeguarding Information For Parents
Understanding online safety is tricky for all ages. The COVID-19 pandemic means children are online more than ever. Our aim is to share with you advice to help you learn about staying safe online as a family.
Social media and online content is hugely popular and a really valuable resource. However, like everything else, accessing this comes with risks. Whilst not every risk turns out to be a problem, it is our job as parents and carers to help our young people understand the risks and learn how to deal with them, hopefully thereby reducing the likelihood of it turning into a problem.
To find out more about Safeguarding across all the schools within St Thomas Catholic Academies Trust, you can visit STCAT Safeguarding page.
There is lots of useful information available to help us make sure it’s safe for every child to go online. The information below has been taken from www.gov.uk website.
Understand the risks children may need to deal with:
What they might see or do:
Seeing or sharing of violent, sexual and pornographic content
Inaccurate or false information and extreme views
Promotion of harmful behaviours including self-harm, anorexia and suicide
Over-sharing of personal information
Actively or unintentionally getting involved in bullying or hurtful behaviour
Who they might meet:
People who might bully, intimidate or frighten
People posing behind fake profiles for:
Sexual grooming and stalking
Blackmail and extortion
Identity theft and hacking
How this could affect them:
Fear of missing out leading to excessive use or exaggeration
Getting upset by things they have seen and being uncertain about what to do
Engaging, or being pressured into engaging in more risky behaviour either by accident or by design
Developing unrealistic, and perhaps depressing ideals of body image and gender
Becoming subject to peer pressure or interactions that are intense or too difficult to handle
Creating an online reputation that may create problems for them in the future
Practical tips to help minimise the risks your child might face
Ask them to show you which social media apps they use and what they like about them. Talk about how they use them and what makes them so engaging
Explain how you can use privacy settings to make sure only approved friends can see posts & images
Check if any of their apps have ‘geo-location’ enabled, sharing their location unintentionally
Show them how to report offensive comments or block people who upset them
Check ‘tagging’ settings so that when others are posting or sharing photos online, your child’s identity is not revealed. Also, get people‘s consent before sharing photos
Encourage your child to come and talk to you if they see anything that upsets them
Keep talking and stay involved
Encourage your child to think carefully about the way they, and others behave online, and how they might deal with difficult situations.
People may not always be who they say they are online: how can this create problems?
Why is it unwise to meet anyone in the real world that you’ve only ever met online?
Even if you think your messages are private, remember that words and images can always be captured and broadcast.
People present themselves differently online - do they really look like that? Are they always having that good a time?
Be aware that screens, and especially being anonymous, can lead people to say things they wouldn’t say to someone’s face.
What does being a good friend and a likeable person online look like?
There can be pressure to be part of a particular group online or to be seen to be following a certain set of ideas
How can you take a step back and make your own decisions?
You can find out more about how children use social media, the apps they use, the risks they face, how to use privacy settings, and advice and tips about how to talk to your children at:
www.childnet.com/sns
www.internetmatters.org
www.nspcc.org.uk/onlinesafety
www.parentzone.org.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Mission Team - Holy Family Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Mission Team
Holy Family's Mission Team is made up of sixteen dedicated Year 6 children, who enjoy living out the Gospel values and set an example to us all of how to live as Christ's disciples here on earth. These children meet weekly with our RE lead, Mrs O'Reilly, where they spend time planning prayer and liturgy for our school. They visit classes weekly, in order to share the Word of God with all children. They are also very involved in our weekly liturgies, as well as larger-scale celebrations with Fr Tony.
The members of our Mission Team attend annual training with other children from our local schools, to ensure that they are keeping their skills sharp! Members of the Mission Team also contribute to our weekly whole school newsletter, usually exploring the scripture they have shared:
Hi, I’m Francesca, the Faith Ambassador for Reception (Mrs Scott’s Class). This week’s Wednesday word is FAITHFULNESS. In this week’s Gospel, Jesus describes the earth-shaking signs of Jesus’ return to us all. He reminds us that to look beyond the worries and bad moments of our life and world, we have to stay faithful, and we know every step we take God is always with us.
Here is the Gospel story taken from the book of Mark.
Jesus said to his disciples, “A time will come when I will return and appear in the clouds with power and glory. Then I will send my angels to gather my people from every part of the world. Heaven and earth will pas away, but my words will never pass away-they will remain forever”.
Everybody wants a faithful friend and we all have a least one, that is Jesus. He promises to be ours. He is encouraging the disciples (and us) to be faithful to him. A faithful person is gift no money can buy. This week try to be that faithful person that Jesus wanted us to be.
Hello, my name is Kian, and I am a Faith Ambassador. My role is to spread the word of the Gospel with the whole school and each term we get assigned a different class. We say FAITH IS FUN! This week’s Wednesday Word is gift! Our Gospel story this week is from the book of Mark 12:38-44. After each Gospel we say a prayer “Lord Jesus we have listened carefully to your words. Please help us to share the good news of this week’s gospel with our families, through our actions and our words. Amen.”
Hollie writes for us:
Our Wednesday Word this week is FOLLOW. It is important that we all make the right choice about who or what we follow in life. Jesus invites each of us to make following him our most important priority.
In the Holy Gospel, Jesus tells Peter and his friends to sail out in deep water and let down their nets. They had already been fishing all night and had caught nothing but they did as Jesus said and caught many fish. Peter and the fisherman left everything and followed Jesus. This is a clear example of Jesus telling us to follow and make the right choice.
Choosing to follow Jesus may not be easy, but making life better for everyone around us helps make the world a better place.
Your mission: How can you follow Jesus?...Be kind and go out of your way to make others feel welcome and wanted.
